text.title: css-in-js Core Rules
text.summary: Eight testable rules for picking and operating CSS-in-JS in 2026 React stacks.

rule.statement: On React Server Components (Next 13+ App Router, Remix RSC), choose a zero-runtime library: vanilla-extract, Panda CSS, Linaria. Do NOT use emotion or styled-components in RSC trees.
rule.rationale: Runtime CSS-in-JS does not work in Server Components — the styles cannot be serialised across the server/client boundary, leading to FOUC or build errors. Zero-runtime libs extract styles at build time.

rule.statement: Runtime CSS-in-JS (emotion, styled-components) is acceptable ONLY in pure client SPAs without RSC.
rule.rationale: Runtime libraries provide ergonomic dynamic styling at the cost of runtime overhead. That cost is fine in client SPAs, prohibitive in RSC.

rule.statement: Declare `styled` components at module scope, never inside React render functions. Define once, reuse across renders.
rule.rationale: Defining styled inside render creates a new component class per render, defeating memoisation and triggering full re-mount of the styled subtree.

rule.statement: Use transient props (`$primary`) for styling props so they are not forwarded to the underlying DOM element.
rule.rationale: Non-transient styling props leak to the DOM as invalid HTML attributes and trigger React warnings. `$prefix` keeps them in JS land.

rule.statement: Augment the library's theme type via `declare module "styled-components" { export interface DefaultTheme extends MyTheme {} }` so `theme.color.primary` is type-safe.
rule.rationale: Without augmentation, `theme` is `any`; refactors silently break theme references. Augmentation makes the theme part of the type system.

rule.statement: When the project is React with TypeScript and the CSS-in-JS decision is open or under audit, the decision MUST be taken on a named trigger - a new stack decision, or an audit opened by a router change such as adopting the Next App Router - and MUST produce the 02-output-contract record with `library`, `runtime_kind`, `uses_rsc` and `theme_type_augmented`, where `uses_rsc` is read from the framework configuration (App Router or Remix RSC present), `uses_rsc == true` forces `runtime_kind == "zero"`, and `library` names exactly one of the enum values - never two libraries in one bundle.

rationale.source: Next.js docs - Styling: CSS-in-JS (App Router); React docs - Server Components

rule.rationale: Next.js documents that runtime CSS-in-JS libraries are not supported in Server Components, so the router choice, not team preference, decides the `runtime_kind`. Reading `uses_rsc` from the config and pinning the decision to a trigger is what stops fm-01 (emotion in an RSC tree) and fm-05 (two libraries in one app) from arriving one import at a time.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but the record cannot be produced - `uses_rsc` is undecidable because the framework or router is not yet chosen, `library` would need two values because styled-components and emotion are both in the bundle, or no theme type exists yet so `theme_type_augmented` cannot be evaluated - the decision MUST block and name the missing input (router decision, single-library decision, or theme type), and MUST NOT emit a record with `uses_rsc` guessed or `library` set to `none` as a placeholder.
rule.rationale: A guessed `uses_rsc: false` validates against the schema and licenses a runtime library that breaks the moment the App Router lands. `library: none` as a placeholder is indistinguishable from a genuine no-CSS-in-JS decision, so the audit that should reopen the question never fires.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - Tailwind / utility-first CSS used exclusively, a non-React project (Vue / Svelte / Solid), or a site shipping zero client JS - the methodology MUST NOT be applied; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor from Prerequisites (ticket, commit or ADR URL) naming the failed precondition and the route taken instead (`best-practices-2026` for the React 19 / Next 15 baseline, the framework-specific styling methodology for non-React), and MUST NOT be written as a `library: none` record of this methodology.

rationale.source: Tailwind CSS docs; Next.js docs - Styling

rule.rationale: A Tailwind-only or non-React project has no `runtime_kind` to decide, and a `none` record would let the next React migration read the question as already settled. Anchoring the skip to the ticket keeps the decision reopenable at the moment the preconditions change.
